content:
This is the chapter your child will use for the rest of their life: discounts, GST, compound interest. The IMO’s favourite trap sits right in the middle of it — two successive 10% discounts are NOT 20% off. Below sits a free IMO Class 8 Comparing Quantities online test — 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation under every answer. Eight out of ten is the score to beat.

What the IMO asks from Comparing Quantities in Class 8

  • Percentage increase and decrease; successive changes.
  • Marked price, discount and successive discounts.
  • GST and sales-tax bills.
  • Compound interest — annual and half-yearly compounding.
  • CI vs SI comparisons over 2 and 3 years.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Successive discounts multiply: 10% then 10% is 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81 — an 19% cut, not 20%.
  • A = P(1 + r/100)ᵗ does compound interest in one line.
  • Half-yearly compounding: HALVE the rate, DOUBLE the periods.
  • CI − SI over 2 years = P(r/100)² — the interest earned by the first year’s interest.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Adding successive percentage changes instead of multiplying factors.
  • Charging the second year’s interest on the original principal only — that is SI, not CI.
  • Computing discount % on cost price (it stands on the MARKED price).

quiz.title: IMO Class 8 Comparing Quantities Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 8: Comparing Quantities

questions.q: A number is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change?
questions.explanation: Let the number be 100. After 20% increase: 100 × 1.20 = 120. After 20% decrease: 120 × 0.80 = 96. Net change = (96 - 100)/100 × 100 = -4%. Hence a 4% decrease.

questions.q: An article is sold at a discount of 20% on the marked price and still there is a profit of 20%. If the cost price is Rs 500, what is the marked price?
A retailer buys a fan for Rs 1,500 and marks it 40% above the cost price. He then offers a 25% discount. Find the profit percent.
A TV set costs Rs 15,000 before tax. If 18% GST is charged, what is the total amount to be paid?
The difference between CI and SI on a certain sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs 50. Find the sum.
questions.explanation: For 2 years, CI - SI = P x (r/100)². So P x (10/100)² = 50. P x 0.01 = 50. P = Rs 5,000.

questions.q: A sum of Rs 15,625 amounts to Rs 17,576 in 3 years at compound interest compounded annually. Find the rate.
The population of a town is 50,000 and it increases at 4% per annum. What will the population be after 2 years?
If the price of sugar rises by 25%, by what percentage must a household reduce consumption so that expenditure remains unchanged?
A merchant marks goods 80% above CP. He sells half at 20% discount and the rest at 40% discount. Find the overall profit percent.
questions.explanation: Let total CP = 200 (each half = 100, MP for each = 180). SP first half: 180 × 0.80 = 144. SP second half: 180 × 0.60 = 108. Total SP = 252. Profit = 52. Profit% = 52/200 × 100 = 26%.

questions.q: A manufacturer sells goods worth Rs 1,50,000 at 18% IGST to a wholesaler. The wholesaler adds 20% margin and sells inter-state at 18% IGST. What IGST must the wholesaler remit?
